what: Norfolk Southern runs a freight railroad across the eastern United States, moving coal, chemicals, cars, metals and intermodal containers over about 19,000 route miles from the Atlantic coast to the Midwest.
customers: Manufacturers, chemical and energy producers, carmakers and intermodal logistics companies.
money: chemicals, agriculture, metals, automotive and forest products
containers and trailers moved for logistics companies and ports
moat: Rights of way across the eastern US that could not be assembled again, leaving only two railroads serving the region.
risks: Revenue has been flat as coal declines and industrial demand softens
The 2023 East Palestine derailment left large costs and regulatory scrutiny
Rail mergers elsewhere could change the competitive map
Service problems invite shipper complaints and regulatory action
opportunities: Cost discipline has lifted operating margins back above 35%
New industrial plants along its network create fresh freight
Rail remains far cheaper than trucking for long-distance bulk movement
watch: The operating ratio and intermodal volumes.
